summary:
**Space Journey** is an interactive educational website that brings the stories of NASA’s robotic explorers and the equipment they left behind on Mars to life.

Our project focuses on NASA’s **Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity rovers**, three explorers that transformed our understanding of Mars. Through interactive timelines, mission information, photographs, scientific discoveries, and exploration stories, users can follow each rover’s journey from launch and landing to their final days on the Martian surface.

Instead of simply presenting technical data, Space Journey turns NASA’s mission records into an engaging digital story. Users can explore where the rovers traveled, what they discovered, the challenges they faced, and what remains of them on Mars today.

By combining NASA’s official data and imagery with interactive storytelling, Space Journey aims to help people understand that even after a spacecraft stops operating, its discoveries and legacy continue to shape our exploration of the Solar System.
details:
Space Journey is an interactive educational website that tells the story of NASA’s Mars exploration through the journeys of the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, as well as other Mars exploration missions. Instead of presenting the information as a traditional collection of facts, the project turns mission data, photographs, discoveries, and timelines into an interactive experience where users can explore the history and legacy of these robotic explorers.

What does it do and how does it work?

Users can navigate through the website to learn about the rovers, their missions, scientific instruments, discoveries, journeys, and eventual mission endings. The website organizes complex NASA information into accessible sections with interactive navigation, images, and mission storytelling.

The project uses NASA information and imagery to connect the technical details of each rover with the human story of exploration: where the rover went, what it encountered, what it discovered, and what remains on Mars after the mission ended.

What benefits does it have?

Space Journey makes space science easier and more engaging to explore, especially for students and people who may not have a technical background. Instead of requiring users to read lengthy scientific documents, the website presents the information visually and interactively.

It also helps users understand that when a spacecraft stops operating, its scientific legacy does not disappear. The data and discoveries collected by these missions continue to contribute to our understanding of Mars.

Intended impact

Our goal is to increase public interest in planetary science and space exploration while helping users appreciate the scientific and historical significance of equipment left behind on other worlds.

We want visitors to see these machines not simply as abandoned hardware, but as explorers that carried out important scientific missions and became part of humanity's history of exploring another planet.

Tools and technologies

We developed the project as a web application using:

  • HTML — website structure and content
  • CSS — visual design, layout, and responsive styling
  • JavaScript — interactive functionality and dynamic elements
  • NASA data and imagery — scientific information, mission history, photographs, and exploration records
  • GitHub/GitHub Pages — project version control and website deployment

The project was designed as a browser-based experience, so users do not need specialized hardware or software to explore it.

What makes the project creative?

The creative aspect of Space Journey is the way we transform scientific mission records into an interactive story. Rather than simply listing specifications and discoveries, we present the rover missions as journeys.

The website allows users to move through the exploration story and understand the relationship between the rover, its environment, its scientific discoveries, and its eventual mission ending.

This approach combines science, technology, visual storytelling, and interactive web design to make NASA's exploration history more accessible.

Factors considered by our team

We considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, visual presentation, ease of navigation, and the importance of using reliable NASA sources. We also considered how to present a large amount of scientific information without overwhelming users.

Another important consideration was the project's connection to the challenge theme. We wanted to show that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its story. Spirit and Opportunity may no longer be operating, but their discoveries, data, and physical presence on Mars remain part of humanity's exploration history.
